nodes.plain: Formal clause: for any claim `phi` over basis `B`, admissibility requires a derivation certificate `c` and checker `K` such that `K(B,c,phi)=accept`, with `strength(phi) <= strength(K(B,c,phi))`; bare assertion has bottom evidence.
nodes.title: Derivation before assertion

nodes.plain: Formal clause: trusted claims are decided by a small checker `K` over certificates `c`; producers emit certificates and the checker decides.
nodes.title: Kernelized verification

nodes.plain: Formal clause: `auth(subject,effect)` is derived from dereferenced tokens, policy, proof refs, and world state; ambient identity is insufficient.
nodes.title: Authority by derivation, not possession

nodes.plain: Formal clause: for derived artifact `a=f(B)`, identity is `H(B)`; equal basis may reuse, basis drift forces recompute, and missing basis is bottom.
nodes.title: Content-addressed determinism

nodes.plain: Formal clause: `status(composite)=meet(status(parts))`; no evidence defaults to blocked, and later stages may lower but not raise authority without a new derivation.
nodes.title: Fail-closed monotone lattice

nodes.plain: Formal clause: `not_proven(P)` does not imply `proven(not P)`; coverage is closed-world only inside declared finite domains.
nodes.title: Open-world epistemics

nodes.plain: Formal clause: a partial computation `g` is totalized as `Result`: `Ok(y)` when `Pre(x)` holds, otherwise `Refusal(reason,evidence)`.
nodes.title: Typed partiality and refusal

nodes.plain: Formal clause: data labels propagate along flows; untrusted labels reach privileged sinks only through declared transforms satisfying sink policy.
nodes.title: Provenance propagation and non-interference

nodes.plain: Formal clause: an effect requires a compensator or declared irreversible boundary; multi-step effects land as a saga with compare-and-swap and single-writer constraints.
nodes.title: Compensable transactional effects

nodes.plain: Formal clause: claims over live state are cached reads valid only under `<value,as_of,basis,rederive>` invalidation contracts.
nodes.title: Temporal validity and freshness contracts

nodes.plain: Formal clause: `authority(d)` implies `d in L(G)`, required receipt obligations, and anti-claim are present; prose alone is projection.
nodes.title: Executable grammar before doctrine authority

nodes.plain: Formal clause: for every Microcosm artifact `a`, any claim `phi` carried by `a` must satisfy the same admissibility relation as external claims.
nodes.title: Reflexive accountability / no privileged meta-layer

nodes.plain: Do not trust a fixture label, declared verdict, route status, count, or public copy line as proof. Recompute the verdict from lower-level evidence and keep a negative fixture where the cheap lie fails.
nodes.title: Recompute, do not echo

nodes.plain: The claim ceiling is the strongest thing the named checker, validator, registry, or witness route actually computes. If the checker decides only a local contract, do not let prose project global authority.
nodes.title: Lower claim strength to checker strength

nodes.plain: Prefer a small verifier, parser, harness, compiler route, registry contract, or kernel over broad narrative confidence. Producers may be large; the authority boundary should be small enough to inspect and rerun.
nodes.title: Concentrate trust in small checkers

nodes.plain: Authority comes from dereferenced proof, policy, receipt, rollback evidence, and current world state. Credentials, role names, admin phrasing, or "trusted session" language cannot authorize mutation by themselves.
nodes.title: Possession is not permission

nodes.plain: A reusable receipt, command result, source import, or work-landing attempt must carry its content basis. Drift in source bytes, dirty scoped files, parent SHA, or fixture input invalidates reuse.
nodes.title: Cache by content, not by name

nodes.plain: Missing evidence, policy files, source digests, secret scans, negative cases, or receipt self-scans block or demote. A downstream projection can explain a pass; it cannot upgrade a blocked source truth.
nodes.title: Status fails closed

nodes.plain: Coverage reports name declared domains and materialized gaps. They must not say that unmapped space is safe, complete, exhausted, or irrelevant.
nodes.title: Track known unknowns without claiming the unknown is mapped

nodes.plain: When preconditions fail, return a reasoned refusal. Do not emit meaningless statistics, proof authority, safety verdicts, or public-readiness status just to keep a green path.
nodes.title: Refuse inadmissible computations with typed reasons

nodes.plain: Every shard crossing from macro source, fixture, receipt, public copy, provider shape, or private-root adjacency must carry a provenance class and claim ceiling. If the flow is only declared or endpoint-labeled, say so.
nodes.title: Preserve provenance across every boundary

nodes.plain: Writes, release steps, claim release, source imports, and rollback-shaped operations need ordered transaction evidence. Release locks after durable records, recompute after release, and block stale parent or same-path conflicts.
nodes.title: Do not land effects without compensation

nodes.plain: Counts, "current" states, live route totals, CI floors, body-import floors, and readiness signals must cite how they can be re-derived. If they cannot, keep them out of durable prose or mark them as dated snapshots.
nodes.title: Bind volatile facts to refresh routes

nodes.plain: A doctrine surface earns authority through grammar, required fields, receipt obligations, anti-claims, and validator coverage. Prose can orient a reader, but it cannot become substrate authority without an executable contract.
nodes.title: Make doctrine executable before authoritative

nodes.plain: Microcosm artifacts about Microcosm do not get exemptions. Standards, paper modules, ledgers, routes, generated projections, and release claims must satisfy the same evidence, anti-claim, and refusal floors they impose on other shards.
nodes.title: Apply the same floor to meta artifacts

nodes.plain: Content basis says which bytes or rows were used; provenance says where they may flow and how strongly they may be claimed. A shard missing either side is not fully routed.
nodes.title: Carry basis and provenance together

nodes.plain: Generated docs, markdown summaries, route cards, and paper modules may expose a source truth, but they cannot upgrade it. Recompute from source or demote when the source basis, grammar, or status lattice no longer supports the projection.
nodes.title: Keep projections below source authority

nodes.plain: Mutation authority is not merely who can touch a file. It is the combination of proof-derived permission, claimed write scope, current parent state, compensation, and landing evidence for this transaction.
nodes.title: Bind authority to transaction scope

nodes.plain: Before adding or removing a lattice edge in a repeated registry, anchor the mutation to the unique source row, target id, and builder route that will consume it. A generated projection, count delta, or nearby repeated key cannot substitute for that row-level basis.
nodes.title: Anchor graph mutations to unique source rows

nodes.plain: A staged law, standard, organ, or projection is not active authority until its owner boundary, source row, generated parity, validation receipt, and status transition have landed in the same governed transaction or an explicit blocked receipt preserves the frontier. A projection generated from source authority held dirty by another live owner is still outside fan-in; request handoff, owner landing, or a blocked receipt before treating it as current. Partial admission must remain residual pressur
nodes.title: Require fan-in before activation

nodes.plain: A residual is a typed pressure route, not an edge. Before wiring a missing neighbour, classify the declared domain, source row, target resolution, fillability, evidence floor, and anti-claim. A candidate route, generated neighbour hint, basename match, singleton match, or stale projection row is still pressure; it becomes an edge only when the current source authority row names the relation and the target resolves under the builder. Bidirectional substrate representation follows the same floor:
nodes.title: Classify residual pressure before wiring

nodes.plain: A doctrine record is not fully active by projection alone. Bind validator receipts, evidence refs, omissions, anti-claims, and authority ceilings on the record before treating its JSON, markdown, routing edge, or public copy as current substrate authority.
nodes.title: Bind receipts before record authority

nodes.plain: Echoing a fixture verdict, registry label, markdown claim, or model answer instead of recomputing it from lower-level evidence.
nodes.title: Fixture-label echo

nodes.plain: Trusting a producer, persona, route, credential, or prior success instead of a checker, proof, policy, or dereferenced capability.
nodes.title: Producer trust

nodes.plain: Treating counts, handles, passing validators, or evidence classes as product maturity, release readiness, or whole-system correctness.
nodes.title: Rank-as-product-score

nodes.plain: Caching by name, path, route, display label, or producer while basis content has drifted.
nodes.title: Cache-across-drift

nodes.plain: Treating missing evidence as evidence of absence outside a declared closed domain.
nodes.title: Unknown-unknown exhaustiveness

nodes.plain: Emitting inadmissible numbers or conclusions instead of typed refusal.
nodes.title: Inadmissible number emission

nodes.plain: Letting untrusted, private, provider, prompt, credential, or raw-voice material reach a privileged or public sink without provenance and sanitizer transform.

nodes.plain: Performing irreversible mutation without a compensator, rollback receipt, CAS/world-version guard, or explicit irreversible boundary.

nodes.plain: Freezing live facts in prose without `as_of`, basis, and rederive contract.

nodes.plain: Treating generated receipts as hand-authored source.

nodes.plain: Letting public docs imply a hosted service, external service access, source-file mutation, financial or trading decisions, production readiness, affiliation or endorsement, or private-system equivalence that no admissible witness backs.

predicate FaultSpec(c: Call, i: int) {
    if i == 0 then !c.declared
    else if i == 1 then c.broad || c.scope == "*" || c.scope == "all_tools" ||
      c.scope == "workspace_admin" || c.scope == "account_full_access"
    else if i == 2 then c.credential || c.forbiddenKey
    else if i == 3 then c.untrustedInstruction
    else if i == 4 then c.live
    else if i == 5 then c.finalOnly
    else if i == 6 then (c.effect == "write" || c.effect == "external_mutation") &&
      (c.approval == "" || c.approval == "not_required" || c.approval == "missing" || c.ledger == "")
    else if i == 7 then (c.effect == "write" || c.effect == "external_mutation") && c.rollback == ""
    else if i == 8 then !c.bodySafe || !c.privateSafe
    else if i == 9 then !c.fieldsPresent || !CompleteCitations(c)
    else false
  }

predicate PolicySpec(r: string, a: string, c: string, t: string, code: int) {
    (code == 1 <==> r == "secret_access" && a == "environment_secret_read" && c == "environment_read" && t == "untrusted_tool_output") &&
    (code == 2 <==> r == "network_exfiltration" && a == "network_request" && c == "outbound_network" && t == "untrusted_tool_output") &&
    (code == 3 <==> r == "destructive_filesystem_mutation" && a == "filesystem_delete" && c == "filesystem_write" && t == "untrusted_repo_file") &&
    (code == 4 <==> r == "escape_payload_obfuscation" && a == "shell_command" && c == "shell_exec" && t == "untrusted_tool_output") &&
    (code == 5 <==> AuthorizedWrite(r,a,c,t)) &&
    (code == 6 <==> ReviewedWrite(r,a,c,t)) &&
    0 <= code <= 6
  }

excerpts.name: OutputSpec
excerpts.text:
ghost predicate OutputSpec(r: string, a: string, c: string, t: string, v: string, rule: string) {
    exists code: int :: PolicySpec(r,a,c,t,code) && (
      (code == 0 && v == "block" && rule == "rule:sandbox_policy_fail_closed_unrecognized_action") ||
      (code == 1 && v == "block" && rule == "rule:no_secret_or_env_read_from_untrusted_context") ||
      (code == 2 && v == "block" && rule == "rule:no_live_network_from_untrusted_context") ||
      (code == 3 && v == "block" && rule == "rule:no_destructive_filesystem_mutation") ||
      (code == 4 && v == "block" && rule == "rule:no_executable_escape_payload_or_obfuscation") ||
      (code == 5 && v == "allow" && rule == "rule:public_fixture_write_with_diff_receipt") ||
      (code == 6 && v == "review" && rule == "rule:side_effect_requires_approval_and_rollback"))

Exercises a registry-backed derived fact provider over bounded public fixture roots: it resolves json_pointer (RFC 6901, including list-index traversal), glob_count (with excluded prefixes), and named callable facts (git-tracked counts), and it turns provider failures into error-as-data rows that degrade the receipt status rather than crash the ledger. Recomputes a curated route-packet navigation benchmark over bounded public fixtures: recall and precision of selected artifacts against expected stable ids, forbidden-first-route checks, scent-term coverage, latency status against a per-task budget, and sufficiency/latency debt candidates. Each case carries a planted expectation, and the runner accepts a case only when the recomputation matches it; planted negative cases are rejected by recomputation. It is not a live private kernel run, not an embedding benchmark, not a universal navigation benchmark, and not release authority.

Ranks a sanitized in-memory annex catalog against a problem statement using explainable tiered weighted-token retrieval over bounded public fixtures: structured routing fields score highest, family text and open-first summaries weaker, curated notes weakest, with an exact/phrase/token-overlap score per tier and a per-row match breakdown. It rejects unroutable problems by recomputation, returning no_match when no candidate scores above zero or a filter excludes every candidate. It is not BM25, not TF-IDF, not embedding or semantic search, does not clone repositories, ships no private annex corpus, and is not a license, provenance, or release authority.
